     Beyond Every Summit
Lies a New Horizon
Yet, even as we celebrate these achievements, we recognise them for 
what they truly are: not just the culmination of our journey, but the 
beginning of an even more ambitious chapter. 
However, the climb is far from over, and the horizon before us is 
broader than ever. 
"Beyond Every Summit Lies a New Horizon " is more than the theme 
of this Integrated Annual Report. With every peak we conquer, the 
horizon stretches further, presenting new possibilities for growth, 
innovation, and value creation. And as we reach one horizon, another 
emerges, waiting to be explored.has strengthened our resolve to think bigger, build better and create 
more enduring value. What began as a single aspiration has evolved 
into a diversiﬁed institution that continues to shape skylines, 
communities and the future of urban India. 
FY 26 was one such deﬁning chapter in our journey. 
It was a year in which we reached new milestones in scale and 
performance, expanded our footprint into new geographies, 
established our presence in new markets, and strengthened the 
foundations of a more diversiﬁed and resilient enterprise. It was a year 
that reaﬃrmed the trust placed in the Prestige name and reﬂected the 
strength of a business built with patience, discipline and a long-term 
vision. A summit is often seen as the culmination of a journey. It is where 
ambition meets achievement, where eﬀort ﬁnds reward, and where 
one pauses to reﬂect on how far the climb has been. 
But for those who are driven by purpose, a summit oﬀers something far 
more valuable than a sense of arrival. It oﬀers perspective. 
From every new height, the horizon stretches further than before. New 
possibilities emerge. New challenges beckon. New dreams begin to 
take shape.
That has always been the Prestige way. 
For nearly four decades, we have never allowed success to deﬁne our 
limits. Every milestone has expanded our vision. Every achievement 
Prestige Nautilus, Mumbai
Artists ImpressionThis spirit lives in the people who build with us, the stakeholders who 
place their trust in us, and the many forms of value, including ﬁnancial, 
human, natural and social that we create together for the years ahead. 
Some aspirations are timeless. Like the aspiration to lead the way, 
deliver our best, create new milestones and then surpass the very 
milestones you created to achieve something even more spectacular. 
At Prestige, we make these aspirations come true every single day.
For it is not the summit that deﬁnes the journey. It is the horizon that 
continues to inspire it.

About the Report
The Report brings ﬁnancial results together with the strategic, operational, governance and sustainability factors that shape the Company’s ability 
to grow and remain resilient.
It outlines how we  apply  our  resources and capabilities across the six capitals: Financial, Manufactured, Intellectual, Human, Natural, and Social 
and Relationship, to support our expanding and diversiﬁed portfolio.
Every Prestige development begins with a long-term vision, one that extends beyond completing a project or entering a new market. It is about 
creating places that respond to people’s aspirations, strengthen communities, and contribute to the growth of the cities in which the Company 
operates, while creating and preserving value for all its stakeholders in the short, medium, and long term.
Reporting Scope and Boundary
This Integrated Annual Report ('Report') 
presents the performance of Prestige 
Estates Projects Limited, along with our 
subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates 
(also referred to as ‘Prestige’, the 
‘Company’, the ‘Group’ or ‘we’), unless 
stated otherwise in the relevant section, 
for the period from April 1, 2025 to March 
31, 2026.
This Report covers our key business The Management has reviewed and approved this Integrated Annual 
Report. In doing so, it has considered information generated through 
the Company’s internal reporting systems, management processes, 
and consultations with relevant business functions.
Based on this review, the Management believe that the Report 
presents a balanced and reliable account of the Company’s material 
ﬁnancial and non-ﬁnancial performance during FY 26. Frameworks and Alignment Responsibility Statement
The Report brings together the Company’s ﬁnancial & 
non-ﬁnancial performance. It explains how strategy, project 
execution, customer relationships, employee capabilities, 
governance, environmental performance, and resource use 
aﬀect revenue, proﬁtability, cash ﬂows, risk exposure, and future 
growth. This connectivity enables stakeholders to assess both 
the Company’s reported performance and its ability to sustain 
value creation.
We  follow a deﬁned reporting process to identify, validate, and 
present the information included in the Integrated Annual 
Report. Business functions provide ﬁnancial, operational, and 
sustainability data, which are subject to internal veriﬁcation and 
review by the relevant leadership teams.
We then assess the information through the lens of materiality 
and stakeholder relevance to determine the matters that merit 
inclusion. Management reviews the resulting narrative to ensure 
consistency between the Company’s strategy, performance, 
risks, opportunities and future priorities. Where applicable, 
independent assurance and statutory audit processes further 
strengthen the reliability of the reported information.How this Report is PreparedThis Report is aligned with:

=== page 9 ===
Forty years ago, we set out with a belief that real estate is about more 
than constructing buildings; it is about creating places that stand the 
test of time. What began with a handful of projects in Bengaluru has 
evolved into a national platform spanning multiple asset classes, 
diverse markets and enduring partnerships. Every milestone has 
expanded our horizons and yet keeping us anchored in the values that 
have guided us since day one.In 1986, we embarked on our journey in Bengaluru with Prestige 
Court, our ﬁrst commercial project, before bringing that same 
vision to life through Prestige Oakwood, our maiden residential 
development. Those ﬁrst milestones marked the beginning of a 
legacy built brick by brick; driven by craftsmanship, trust and the 
courage to dream bigger with every project we undertook.Building trust, establishing quality and 
starting the journeyLaying the Foundation
Our JourneyA Legacy
in Motion 
Where It All Began1986 - 1990
As our aspirations grew, so did the institution behind them. We 
transformed from a partnership ﬁrm into a company, creating a 
stronger foundation for the journey ahead. Believing that our 
responsibility extended well beyond project delivery, we 
established our property management and maintenance vertical 
to ensure every Prestige development continued to be cared for 
throughout its lifecycle, preserving quality and creating lasting 
value for our customers.
Projects such as Prestige Four Seasons, Prestige Elgin, Prestige 
Poseidon and Prestige Acropolis reﬂected our growing ambition 
and evolving capabilities. By the close of the decade, we had 
completed nearly 60 projects, while our annual sales remained 
below ₹1,000 mn, a humble beginning that would pave the way 
for far greater milestones in the years ahead.Building the Organisation and Scale1991 - 2000With an expanding vision, came an expanding portfolio. We 
entered organised retail with Forum Koramangala, made our 
foray into hospitality with Angsana Oasis Spa & Resort, and 
began extending our presence across southern India, marking 
the start of our journey as a multi-asset, multi-city developer.Entering new asset classes, creating larger developments 
and expanding beyond Bengaluru.Broadening the Vision
Entering New Horizons2001 - 2005
This decade saw us reimagine urban development at a larger 
scale. Landmark developments such as Prestige Shantiniketan, 
UB City, Cessna Business Park and Prestige Golfshire reﬂected 
our growing ambition, while our expansion into Hyderabad, 
Chennai and Kochi, and our partnership with CapitaLand 
Singapore, strengthened our national footprint. By the end of the 
decade, we had delivered our 100th project, with annual sales 
approaching ₹20,000 mn.Creating Integrated Landmarks2006 - 2010Strengthening institutional depth, widening 
geography and adding marquee assets.Building Institutional Momentum
Building Institutional Strength2011 - 2020
The past few years have marked the beginning of our next phase 
of growth. We unlocked capital through the monetisation of 
select commercial and retail assets, entered the NCR residential 
market, and strengthened our balance sheet through a ₹50,000 
mn qualiﬁed institutional placement. We also launched and 
expanded our ﬂagship “The Prestige City” across four cities 
while continuing to scale our Commercial, Retail and Hospitality 
portfolios.
By the end of this milestone period, we had crossed the 300th
project mark and reached a peak market capitalisation of 
approximately ₹850,000 mn. From our ﬁrst developments in 
Bengaluru to a diversiﬁed national platform, every chapter of 
our journey has laid the foundation for the next and the 
horizon ahead has never looked more promising.Building a National Platform2021 - 2026Our listing in October 2010 opened a new chapter of growth, 
supported by multiple public-market issuances and partnerships 
with leading international private equity investors. We emerged 
as a national real estate developer by entering Pune and the 
Mumbai Metropolitan Region, expanding hospitality through 
Conrad, Sheraton and JW Marriott, and taking on the Delhi 
Aerocity hotel and convention development. Alongside 
completing Prestige Golfshire, we consolidated our retail 
platform, moved into Prestige Falcon Towers, completed our 
200th project and grew annual sales to nearly ₹50,000 mn.
horizon ahead has never looked more promising.

The Only

Stable Credit RatingICRA A+ Founded in Bengaluru in 1986, we have grown from a regional 
developer into a nationally recognised real estate institution with a 
presence across some of India's most signiﬁcant property markets, 
including Bengaluru, Mumbai, NCR, Hyderabad, Chennai, Pune, Kochi 
etc. This measured expansion has been guided by a disciplined 
approach to capital allocation, deep market understanding and a 
persistent focus on execution.
Over the years, we have built an integrated development platform that 
spans the entire real estate lifecycle. From identifying high-potential 
opportunities and conceptualising distinctive developments to 
delivering projects on schedule and managing completed assets, our 
diversiﬁed operating model has enabled us to create sustainable value 
while responding to evolving customer preferences and changing 
market dynamics.Today, our portfolio extends beyond "just buildings". It encompasses 
vibrant residential communities, Grade A oﬃce developments, 
destination retail centres, premium hospitality assets and integrated 
mixed-use developments that contribute meaningfully to the growth of 
India's cities. Every project reﬂects our long-standing commitment to 
quality, transparency, innovation and customer satisfaction.
We don’t just create world-class spaces; we craft environments that

well-being, and stand the test of time.

Our expansion strategy has been centred on India's 
strongest economic and urban growth corridors. Beginning 
in Bengaluru, we have steadily expanded our footprint 
across southern and western India before entering the 
National Capital Region, strengthening our position as a 
truly national developer. 
This diversiﬁed geographic presence provides us with 
access to multiple demand drivers while reducing 
dependence on any single market. It also enables us to 
leverage regional expertise, customer insights and 
execution capabilities across varied asset classes and 
locations. 
Importantly, the breadth of our footprint facilitates the 
exchange of best practices, design innovations and 
successful development concepts across markets, allowing 
us to continually enrich our oﬀerings and introduce proven 
ideas that enhance the customer experience in every 
geography.

an achievement that reﬂects years of dedication, and an invitation to

Beyond Every Summit
Lies a New Horizon 
Dear Stakeholders, Residential demand continues to be driven by genuine end-user 
aspirations, rising incomes and growing conﬁdence in organised 
developers. Commercial real estate remains buoyant as India 
strengthens its position as the preferred destination for Global 
Capability Centres and multinational corporations. Organised Retail is 
beneﬁting from rising consumption and changing consumer 
preferences, while Hospitality is witnessing sustained momentum, 
supported by increasing business travel, tourism and the country's 
expanding global relevance. Collectively, these structural tailwinds 
position India's real estate sector as one of the country's most 
compelling long-term growth stories.
Against this backdrop, Prestige delivered its strongest performance 
yet. 
We achieved our highest-ever annual sales, surpassing ₹300,000 mn, 
marking a historic milestone in our journey, alongside record 
collections and cash ﬂows. These results reﬂect not only strong 
demand, but also the ﬁnancial discipline and execution capability that 
have deﬁned Prestige for nearly four decades. More importantly, they 
reﬂect the continued trust our customers, partners and investors place 
in our brand.
Beyond the numbers, FY 26 expanded the canvas of our business. Our 
maiden residential launch in the National Capital Region, The Prestige 
City Indirapuram, recorded sales of over ₹95,000 mn in its ﬁrst year-  
almost a third of our annual sales and a powerful validation of the 
Prestige brand beyond our traditional strongholds.
Equally signiﬁcant was the completion of our maiden developments in 
Mumbai, another step towards becoming a truly national real estate 
company. Together, these two markets meaningfully broaden our 
growth opportunities for the years ahead.
Even as these milestones deﬁne FY 26, they represent only one part of 
a much larger story.
Over the years, we have deliberately built a diversiﬁed real estate 
platform spanning residential, oﬃce, retail, hospitality and property 
management. Each of these businesses has evolved with a clear 
strategic purpose, collectively serving as multiple engines of growth 
that reinforce one another across economic cycles.
Perhaps the most exciting transformation underway today is the rapid 
expansion of our annuity business.
Across our Commercial Oﬃce portfolio, several marquee 
developments are taking shape in Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi-NCR, 
Chennai, and Kochi. Supported by strong leasing momentum and 
healthy occupier demand, these assets will progressively become 
operational over the next few years, signiﬁcantly expanding our 
recurring rental income. As this portfolio matures, it will create a 
stronger, more resilient earnings proﬁle while establishing a portfolio of 
institutional-quality Grade A oﬃce assets that will serve as a long-term 
engine of value creation for the Group. 
Our Retail platform is witnessing a similarly exciting phase of growth. 
As India's consumption story continues to strengthen,  our destination 
malls are consistently attracting leading global and domestic brands 
while delivering compelling experiences for millions of visitors each 
year. With several new malls under development across multiple cities, 
we expect our Retail segment to emerge as an increasingly meaningful 
contributor to our annuity portfolio.
Hospitality represents another exciting pillar of our long-term strategy. 
Our landmark luxury hospitality development at Delhi Aerocity, 
featuring globally renowned hotel brands, is progressing well and is 
expected to become operational during FY 27. Beyond this, we have 
an exciting pipeline of hospitality developments across Bengaluru, 
Mumbai, Hyderabad, Chennai, Sakleshpur and Goa, reﬂecting our 
long-term conviction in India's rapidly growing travel and tourism 
ecosystem. As these assets progressively come on stream, they will 
signiﬁcantly expand our room inventory, strengthen our recurring 
income base and establish one of the country's most distinguished 
hospitality portfolios. A Year of Historic Growth & Achievements 
The future we envision is backed by strong fundamentals. Today, we 
are executing one of the largest and most diversiﬁed development 
pipelines in our history across India's leading cities. We continued to 
strengthen this pipeline through disciplined business development 
during the year, adding strategically located projects that will support 
sustained growth. Equally encouraging is our substantial sold but 
unrecognised revenue of ₹659,353 mn, which provides exceptional 
visibility into future revenue recognition and earnings, underpinning 
our ﬁnancial performance in the years ahead. Expanding our Growth Horizons 
Growth for us, has never come at the cost of responsibility. Safety and

FY 26 was another deﬁning year for India. Despite an increasingly

A Year of Stellar Performance.
A Future of Greater Possibilities.It was a landmark year in Prestige’s performance as we achieved our 
highest-ever annual sales of ₹300,245 mn, recording a 76.38% 
year-on-year increase, with 22.28 mn sft sold across 11,692 units. As 
sales gathered pace, collections followed with equal strength, reaching 
a record ₹185,146 mn and growing by 53.22% over the previous year. 
This performance strengthened our cash ﬂows and gave us greater 
conﬁdence to advance our development plans. New launches were 
central to this progress. During the year, we introduced 31.84 mn sft of 
projects with an estimated GDV of ₹273,504 mn. 
The market response was immediate, with these launches generating 
sales of ₹173,422 mn and reﬂecting strong customer acceptance and 
sales velocity. Alongside expansion, we maintained our focus on 
execution, delivering 18.22 mn sft across residential and commercial 
developments.
Building on this foundation, we have strengthened our business 
development pipeline with projects carrying an estimated GDV of over 
₹514,200 mn across Bengaluru, Mumbai, NCR, Hyderabad and 
Chennai. This positions us to deepen our national presence and 
pursue the next phase of growth with scale, discipline and purpose. 
FY 26 was a year of breakthrough ﬁnancial performance. Supported by 
momentum and sustained customer conﬁdence, we converted 
operational scale into stronger revenue, proﬁtability and cash 
generation, while further reinforcing the ﬁnancial foundation for our 
next phase of growth. 
This momentum was reﬂected in revenue, which grew by 70.58% 
year-on-year to ₹131,955 mn, EBITDA increased by 43.27% to ₹42,192 
mn with the EBITDA margin standing at 31.97%. This stronger operating 
performance, in turn, ﬂowed through to the bottom line, driving Proﬁt 
After Tax to ₹13,054 mn more than double the previous year and 
reﬂecting a growth of 111.61%.Operational Resilience and Strength
Robust Financial PerformanceThe residential business continued to be our primary growth engine, 
supported by strong demand across Bengaluru, Mumbai, Hyderabad, 
Chennai and our successful expansion into NCR. As a brand that is 
inspired by evolving customer aspirations, our strategy remains 
centred on creating thoughtfully designed communities that combine 
quality, lifestyle and long-term value for customers.
At the same time, our annuity businesses continued to expand and 
create avenues for sustainable revenue generation, reinforcing the 
resilience of our operating model.
Our oﬃce portfolio recorded healthy leasing momentum during the 
year while maintaining occupancy levels above 92%, reﬂecting 
sustained demand from Global Capability Centres, technology 
companies and leading domestic corporates.
Our retail portfolio continued to perform exceptionally well with 
occupancy levels of approximately 99%, while retailers operating 
within our malls recorded gross turnover exceeding ₹25,671 mn during 
the year, aﬃrming the strength of our destination-led retail assets and 
evolving consumer preferences.
Our hospitality business also maintained healthy momentum, 
supported by strong ARRs and Occupancies, improving travel demand 
and continued focus on operational eﬃciencies.Crafting New Urban Destinations
Performance at this scale means little without safety and sustainability. 
We closed FY 26 with a 0% injury rate across our operations, reﬂecting 
our unwavering commitment to the health and safety of our workforce. 
During the year, Prestige 101 and The Prestige, Mumbai achieved a 
5-Star GRESB rating for the second consecutive year, with their score 
improving from 97 to 99, placing these developments among the top 
20% of real estate assets globally and ﬁrst in Asia in the Oﬃce and 
Development category. Across our broader portfolio, 18 developments 
now hold LEED Gold or Platinum certiﬁcation, underscoring our 
commitment to creating world-class, environmentally responsible and 
resource-eﬃcient spaces. Our community programmes reached over 
335,000+ beneﬁciaries during the year, creating meaningful and 
lasting impact. Together, these achievements reinforce our 
commitment to building responsibly, enhancing resilience and creating 
enduring value for all our stakeholders.Building Responsibly
While FY 26 was a year of exceptional performance, it was equally 
focused on investing for the future.
We continued to deploy capital towards strategic land acquisitions and 
business development opportunities across our key markets. These 
investments, though requiring meaningful upfront capital, signiﬁcantly 
strengthen our launch pipeline for the coming years and provide 
long-term visibility of growth. Many of these projects are already 
progressing through planning, design and regulatory approvals and 
are expected to progressively enter the market over the next few 
quarters.
Simultaneously, several of our large-scale commercial oﬃce and retail 
developments are approaching completion, reﬂecting the maturity of

enhance recurring cash ﬂows and strengthen the stability of our 
business.Building a Future-Ready Organisation

connected stages: Mr. Irfan Razack

We follow a transparent governance structure that connects the Board, 
its committees, functional leadership and employees. Our Board 
oversees the design, implementation and monitoring of the risk 
management framework as part of our internal control system, while 
Independent Directors provide objective oversight.
The Risk Management Committee consolidates assessments from 
Committee members and functional heads, reviews exposures beyond 
the Company’s Risk Tolerance and recommends mitigation measures. 
It also oversees the business continuity plan, reviews the Risk 
Management Policy, and monitors ﬁnancial, operational, sectoral, 
sustainability, ESG, information security, and cybersecurity risks.

regulatory developments, climate-related events, project execution 
challenges and cyber threats.
Our Risk Management Policy guides us in evaluating these risks and 
balancing them against potential opportunities. We assess each 
exposure based on its likely impact, expected return and our deﬁned 
Risk Proﬁle. This approach helps us make informed decisions, allocate 
capital prudently, strengthen project delivery and pursue sustainable 
growth.
Functional heads manage risks within their respective areas. They 
identify and assess exposures, implement mitigation measures 
through operating processes and monitor their eﬀectiveness. They 
also report risk events, action plans and progress to support timely 
review, accountability and corrective action.

Risks & Mitigation Measures
Market & Demand Risk
Risk Description Economic slowdown, high interest rates, or weak buyer sentiment may reduce demand across the 
residential, commercial, retail, and hospitality segments. Shifts in customer preferences may increase 
inventory, delay sales and aﬀect revenue, cash ﬂows and rental income. Stronger competition may 
pressure pricing and margins, while limited access to strategically located land may restrict expansion and 
delay launches.
Mitigation Measures
Capitals Impacted UN SDGs ImpactedMarket-led planning:  We track demand, pricing trends and buyer preferences to align product design, 
positioning and launch strategy with market needs.
Product calibration:  We focus on the mid-income segment, where demand remains broad-based, while 
managing exposure to ultra-luxury projects.
Brand diﬀerentiation:  We strengthen our brand, marketing and customer experience to build trust, loyalty 
and market preference.
Portfolio diversiﬁcation:  We expand across residential, commercial, retail and mixed-use developments to 
reduce concentration risk.
Annuity income:  We grow our commercial, retail and mixed-use portfolio to improve recurring income and 
reduce dependence on residential sales.
Land acquisition:  Our Business Development Team evaluates opportunities across markets and helps 
identify and secure suitable land parcels.
Social &
RelationshipFinancialExecution Risk
Risk Description Project delays may damage our reputation, weaken customer conﬁdence and increase disputes. They may 
defer collections, handovers, rentals and operating income, while locking capital in projects and slowing its 
redeployment.
Mitigation Measures
Capitals Impacted UN SDGs ImpactedContractor quality: We appoint reputed contractors with proven execution capabilities to support timely 
delivery, stable cash ﬂows and faster project closure.
Execution oversight:  Our project management teams track progress across locations, while senior 
management reviews sites regularly to identify delays and take timely action.
Digital monitoring: We use project management systems and digital tools to improve coordination, track 
progress and maintain execution schedules.
Social &
RelationshipFinancial
Financial and Liquidity Risk
Risk Description Our launch pipeline, land acquisitions and construction commitments require substantial capital. Any 
mismatch between project spending, customer collections and asset monetisation may strain liquidity and 
delay execution. Higher borrowing costs or an economic slowdown may also aﬀect sales, collections, 
margins and project returns.
Mitigation Measures
Capitals Impacted UN SDGs ImpactedInvestment discipline:  We align project launches, construction spending and land acquisitions with 
demand, collections and available ﬁnancial resources.
Asset monetisation:  We evaluate completed projects and annuity assets for monetisation to unlock capital 
and fund future growth.
Funding ﬂexibility:  We maintain relationships with multiple lenders, explore alternative funding sources 
and manage leverage in line with operating cash ﬂows and collection visibility.
Interest management:  We use ﬁxed-rate borrowings where commercially viable to reduce exposure to 
rising ﬁnance costs.
Market response:  We adjust pricing, payment plans and promotional measures to support sales and 
collections during slower market conditions.
Financial ManufacturedManufactured
Legal Risk
Risk Description Disputes involving customers, vendors or business partners may lead to ﬁnancial loss, operational 
disruption and reputational damage. Failure to meet contractual commitments may result in penalties, 
strained relationships and reduced business credibility. Unclear or contested land titles may delay 
acquisitions and project execution, increase legal costs and lead to prolonged litigation.
Mitigation Measures
Capitals Impacted UN SDGs ImpactedComprehensive due diligence:  We conduct detailed legal reviews before acquiring land or entering into 
material agreements to identify title-related concerns, contractual exposures and other potential legal 
issues. 
Clear contractual framework:  We use well-deﬁned, detailed and enforceable contracts to establish 
responsibilities, reduce ambiguity and minimise the likelihood of disputes. 
Early issue resolution:  We address legal and contractual concerns at an early stage to limit escalation, 
protect stakeholder relationships and reduce potential ﬁnancial and reputational impact.

ESG-Related Risk: Climate, Safety and Compliance
Risk Description Weak ESG integration may expose us to ﬁnancial, operational, regulatory and reputational risks. Extreme 
weather, safety incidents or non-compliance may disrupt projects, increase costs and invite penalties. 
Inadequate ESG performance or disclosure may also weaken stakeholder trust and limit access to 
sustainable ﬁnance.
Mitigation Measures
Capitals Impacted UN SDGs ImpactedSustainable design:  We integrate climate resilience, resource eﬃciency and occupant well-being into 
project planning through recognised green building and wellness standards.
Safety management:  We strengthen workplace safety through a structured management system, regular 
audits, employee training and grievance mechanisms.
ESG oversight:  We track key ESG metrics through a centralised platform, conduct quarterly reviews and 
address performance or compliance gaps.
Stakeholder awareness:  We build ESG awareness across employees and suppliers and improve the 
quality and transparency of stakeholder disclosures.
Cyber, Tech and Data Security Risks
Risk Description
Mitigation Measures
Capitals ImpactedCybersecurity controls:  We apply robust security protocols and conduct regular audits to protect systems, 
data and digital assets.
Technology upgrades:  We modernise our technology environment to improve eﬃciency and remain 
aligned with industry standards.
Recovery readiness:  We maintain disaster recovery and business continuity plans to restore critical 
systems and minimise disruption.Cyberattacks, data breaches or system failures may cause ﬁnancial loss, legal exposure, reputational 
damage and operational disruption. Slow technology adoption may also increase costs, reduce eﬃciency 
and weaken competitiveness.
As the external environment continues to evolve, we remain committed to continuously reviewing and strengthening our risk management 
approach in response to changing market dynamics, regulatory developments, technological advancements and evolving stakeholder 
expectations. Through robust governance, proactive risk identiﬁcation, timely mitigation and disciplined execution, we enhance organisational 
resilience, safeguard stakeholder interests and enable the sustainable creation, preservation and protection of value over the short, medium and 
long term. Social &

EngageOur digital transformation follows a simple principle: information moves 
seamlessly across our business. We connect customer, project, and 
enterprise platforms, replacing fragmented applications and 
document-heavy processes with an integrated, well-governed digital 
ecosystem.
This transformation is based on ﬁve strategic pillars:Our SAP implementation has created a common digital backbone 
across real estate, leasing, retail, property management and 
construction operations, improving speed, consistency and visibility. 
Project creation time has been reduced from nearly two hours to about 
one minute, while standardised cost planning enables faster, more 
consistent execution.
We have also digitised purchase-order-based invoice processing and 
vendor onboarding. Automated workﬂows, source-level data capture, 
and structured approvals have reduced paperwork, improved 
accuracy, and strengthened turnaround time, traceability, and visibility 
across accounts and business teams.With an integrated digital foundation in place, we are extending 
artiﬁcial intelligence across customer engagement and sales. 
AI-enabled voice and chat capabilities allow the Company to respond 
to enquiries around the clock, share relevant project details and move 
interested customers towards the next stage of their journey.We are extending digital insights to the decisions that shape every 
development. By combining geospatial data, immersive visualisation 
and Building Information Modelling, the Company is improving how 
opportunities are evaluated, blueprints are coordinated, and initiatives 
are delivered.
Our AI-powered calling avatar, proactively connects with new leads, 
shares project details, assesses interest and schedules site visits 
directly within the customer relationship management system. During 
major launches, it can engage thousands of prospects simultaneously 
and send timely reminders ahead of scheduled visits.
Available across voice and chat, the agents operate 24/7, with 
response times under 3 seconds and no missed leads. During the year, 
it has handled over 5,000 minutes of conversation, generated more 
than 1,000 leads, scheduled over 250 site visits and supported 37 
bookings.Evaluate
Our AI-enabled land-acquisition intelligence platform digitises the 
land-evaluation lifecycle. Its geospatial capabilities allow teams to 
assess administrative boundaries, transport connectivity and 
site-speciﬁc considerations such as rajakaluves through interactive 
maps.
Automated attribute capture and one-click reporting bring relevant 
information together in a structured format, enabling faster, more 
informed land and site decisions.
Visualise
Our 3D Project visualisation experience that takes users from the wider 
project map to individual ﬂoor plans within a single visual journey 
makes complex project data easier to understand and strengthens 
how developments are presented and perceived.
Deliver
Through NEXTRA, we are creating a connected digital environment for 
initiative delivery-spanning planning, procurement, construction, cost 
control, governance and handover. The programme advances Building 
Information Modelling-led implementation under "The Prestige Way of 
Building 2.0," helping teams coordinate earlier, work from consistent 
project data and strengthen oversight across the development 
lifecycle.
Built on Autodesk Forma and the Autodesk AEC Collection, the 
programme brings diﬀerent asset classes onto a common Design and 
Make platform, with Autodesk Construction Cloud serving as the single 
source of truth.
The information management framework is aligned with ISO 19650 
and supported by the Employer's Information Requirements, BIM 
Execution Plans, and Level of Information Need standards. NEXTRA 
aligns leaders, project teams and ecosystem partners around a shared 
transformation roadmap.
The scale and adoption of the programme during FY 26 are reﬂected 
in the following: 
Understand
Our AI-Driven Customer Interaction Intelligence Framework reviews 
customer interactions to understand engagement, identify intent and 
recommend the next best action. This helps sales teams respond more 
consistently and focus attention where it can create the greatest value.
Improve
Insights generated through our AI-powered customer intelligence, 
CRM, and digital marketing analytics helps sales and marketing teams 
monitor customer journeys, evaluate performance and reﬁne 
engagement strategies. By turning conversations into actionable 
intelligence, we are strengthening responsiveness while building a 
deeper understanding of customer needs.At the centre of the customer ecosystem is PREOSS, our total customer 
experience platform. It connects the My Prestige App, customer 
relationship management system and booking platforms, enabling 
interactions-from enquiry and booking to payment and service-to 
move through a more transparent and engaging journey.
Real-time inventory management and digital-ﬁrst processes further 
support customers and teams with timely, consistent and reliable 
information.Together, PREOSS and SAP form a connected digital core that provides 
customers with greater transparency, enables employees to execute 
faster and improves the reliability of information across the business.Always On. Always Prestige. AI at Prestige

=== page 56 ===
Building Green Spaces
We use LEED, WELL, and IGBC frameworks from the planning stage to 
guide energy eﬃciency, water stewardship, material selection, indoor 
environmental quality and occupant comfort. Our LEED portfolio 
includes 8 Platinum, and 10 Gold certiﬁed projects, while 2 Platinum 
and 3 Gold projects have received pre-certiﬁcation. Prestige Property 
Management and Services also maintains an ISO 14001:2015 certiﬁed 
Environmental Management System, independently veriﬁed by a third 
party, to bring greater discipline and consistency in environmental 
performance across its managed properties. These ratings reﬂect the 
environmental standards embedded across both completed and 
upcoming developments. These frameworks help us improve building 
performance, enhance occupier well-being, strengthen market 
competitiveness and future-proof our portfolio against evolving 
environmental expectations.
We address carbon from the moment we select materials and continue 
through the way we operate completed properties. During 
construction, we increase the use of blended cement and 
supplementary cementitious materials such as GGBS and ﬂy ash, 
together with recycled steel, to reduce the embodied emissions 
associated with conventional materials. We have also piloted 
lower-carbon façade solutions across selected developments, 
balancing emission reduction with durability, quality, and performance.
Once a property becomes operational, we focus on lowering the 
energy it requires each day. High-performance building envelopes, 
eﬃcient HVAC and cooling systems, advanced glazing, energy-saving 
lighting, improved ventilation and daylight-responsive planning help 
reduce demand without compromising occupant comfort. We also 
expand renewable energy sourcing wherever feasible and use 
utility-level monitoring to track consumption, identify ineﬃciencies, and 
improve performance over the life of each asset. Together, these 
measures help in reducing operating costs, improving energy 
eﬃciency, and enhancing the long-term attractiveness of our 
developments.We manage water from the planning stage through construction and 
daily operations, with a clear focus on conserving freshwater, 
improving reuse, and tracking consumption. Detailed commissioning 
plans to set eﬃciency requirements for indoor use, landscaping, and 
building processes. High-eﬃciency ﬁxtures, dual-ﬂush systems, ﬂow 
reducers and leak-detection mechanisms help control demand without 
aﬀecting user comfort. At selected developments, ﬂow reducers can 
lower ﬂow rates by up to 40% while maintaining adequate pressure. 
Eﬃcient water management strengthens resilience in water-stressed 
regions, reduces dependence on freshwater resources, and supports 
the long-term sustainability of our developments.
Across landscaped areas, drip and smart irrigation systems deliver 
water more precisely, while drought-tolerant and low-water species 
reduce irrigation needs. Rainwater-harvesting systems support 
groundwater recharge and provide an additional source for ﬂushing, 
landscaping, basement cleaning, and cooling operations. On-site 
Sewage Treatment Plants treat wastewater for non-potable uses such 
as toilet ﬂushing, landscaping, and dust suppression.
These measures help us reduce freshwater dependence, reuse 
available resources more eﬀectively, and improve resilience across our 
developments.What begins as waste can often be returned as a useful resource. 
Across our sites, teams reuse excavated waste for backﬁlling, turn 
construction debris into pavers and blocks, and adopt reusable 
aluminium formwork and modular methods to reduce material loss. We 
send recyclable and hazardous waste to authorised partners, convert 
organic waste into compost, and recover wood residues from interior 
operations. By keeping materials in use and giving nature room to 
regenerate, we reduce waste while restoring what development can 
place under pressure
Our assessed entities secured a GRESB 5-Star rating in FY 26, marking 
the second consecutive year at this level. The Group’s overall score 
improved from 97 in 2024 to 99 in 2025, placing the assessed entities 
among the top 20% globally and ﬁrst in Asia in the Oﬃce and 
Development category. The recognition reinforces our commitment to 
responsible development and provides investors with independent 
validation of our ESG performance.Water Stewardship Advancing Circularity
We carry the same thinking into the natural environment. Under the 
Prestige Green Promise, we aim to plant one million trees across 
Bengaluru over ten years. The ﬁrst phase has transformed 10 acres, 
with more than 40,000 native saplings planted using the Miyawaki 
method. In FY 26, we planted over 62,000 saplings and committed to 
the ﬁve-year adoption of two tiger cubs at Bannerughatta Biological 
Park, Bengaluru.
Beyond increasing green cover, these initiatives contribute to urban 
biodiversity, strengthen climate resilience and reinforce our

Dr. Rezwan Razack
Joint Managing Director
Born into the entrepreneurial family of Mr. Razack Sattar, 
Rezwan Razack completed his schooling at St.Joseph’s Boys 
High School in Bangalore, graduating in 1971. He earned his 
Bachelor of Commerce (B.Com) degree from St. Joseph’s 
College of Commerce in 1975. His disciplined upbringing, 
academic background, and entrepreneurial values laid the 
foundation for an accomplished future in business.
Rezwan Razack began his career in the family’s retail business 
in 1975, and diversiﬁed into property development in 1985. 
Under his leadership, the Prestige Group has developed over 
330 landmark properties covering residential, commercial, 
retail, hospitality, and mixed-use sectors, spanning nearly 220 
mn sft across India.
Widely respected for his vision, leadership, and ability to build 
high-performing teams, Rezwan has played a deﬁning role in 
shaping the Group’s excellence and expansion in India’s real 
estate landscape.
Together with his distinguished business career, Rezwan 
Razack has devoted nearly six decades to the study, 
preservation, and promotion of Indian Paper Money. What 
began as a youthful fascination evolved into a lifelong 
scholarly pursuit, making him one of the world’s foremost 
authorities on the subject.
His meticulous research, collaborations with collectors and 
institutions worldwide, and unwavering commitment to 
documenting India’s monetary history have culminated in one 
of the most comprehensive collections of Indian banknotes 
ever assembled.
In 2010, he was instrumental in establishing the India Chapter 
of the International Bank Note Society (IBNS) and continues to 
serve as its Chairman.
His lifelong pursuit found permanent expression in Rezwan 
Razack’s Museum of Indian Paper Money, inaugurated in 
Bengaluru in 2020. Recognised as one of the world’s most 
comprehensive museums dedicated exclusively to Indian 
paper money, it preserves and showcases the remarkable 
story of India’s currency through rare banknotes, archival 
material, and thoughtfully curated exhibits.
Rezwan Razack has authored three landmark publications that 
have become important references for collectors, 
researchers, and scholars worldwide:Beyond these books, Rezwan Razack has published 
numerous award-winning research articles on Indian and 
colonial paper money and continues to contribute signiﬁcantly 
to leading numismatic journals globally.
Rezwan Razack’s contributions to numismatics have earned 
him widespread national and international recognition, 
including numerous ‘Lifetime Achievement’ Awards from 
prominent Whole-Time Director numismatic organisations.
In recognition of his exceptional contribution to the ﬁeld, G.D. 
Goenka University conferred upon him the honorary degree 
of Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D. Honoris Causa) in 2021.
In 2025, he created history by becoming the ﬁrst Asian to be 
inducted into the International Bank Note Society (IBNS) Hall 
of Fame in the society’s more than 65-year history, one of the 
highest global honours in the ﬁeld of paper money.
Through his remarkable achievements as a businessman, 
researcher, collector, author, and museum founder, Rezwan 
Razack has created a lasting legacy that preserves India’s 
paper money heritage while inspiring collectors, researchers, 
and future generations across the world.
• ‘The Revised Standard Reference Guide to Indian Paper 
Money’, 2012 - Co-authored as a comprehensive 
reference work on Indian banknotes, it received the IBNS 
Literary Achievement Award - Book of the Year (3rd 
Place) in 2012.
• One Rupee One Hundred Years: 1917-2017 in 2017 - A

India's economy continued to demonstrate structural resilience 
through FY 26, anchored by robust domestic consumption, a 
disciplined ﬁscal trajectory, and a banking system operating 
from a position of strength. According to Provisional Estimates 
released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme 
Implementation (MoSPI), real GDP grew by 7.7% in FY 26, up from 
7.1% in FY 25, while nominal GDP expanded by 8.9% - reaﬃrming 
India's position as one of the world's fastest-growing large 
economies. Growth was broad-based, with the secondary and 
tertiary sectors expanding by 8.8% and 9.3% respectively, and 
sectors including manufacturing and ﬁnancial, real estate and 
professional services registering double-digit growth. Private 
consumption, contributing nearly 60% of GDP, remained the 
primary growth engine, supported by a young and expanding 
workforce with a median age of 28. Gross Fixed Capital 
Formation grew by over 8%, reﬂecting sustained investment-led 
Private consumption 
contributed nearly 60% of GDP 
Domestic demand continued 
to power economic growth.India remained the world's fastest-growing major economy.7.7% GDP GrowthManagement Discussion
& Analysis
momentum and continued infrastructure-led expansion across 
urban corridors. The ﬁnancial sector entered the year in its 
healthiest state in two decades, with non-performing assets at 
multi-year lows and scheduled commercial banks posting record 
proﬁtability of nearly USD 50 billion, enabling sustained credit ﬂow 
into housing and allied sectors. Inﬂation moderated meaningfully 
through the year, opening the door for monetary easing that is 
expected to further catalyse demand across real estate segments. 
Structural tailwinds : rapid digital adoption, expanding 
infrastructure capex, rising manufacturing GDP share, and growing 
global investor conﬁdence (reﬂected in strong PE-VC and FDI 
ﬂows) continued to underpin the medium-term growth outlook. 
Against this macro backdrop, the operating environment for real 
estate through FY 26 was deﬁned by strong economic 
fundamentals even as the sector itself entered a more discerning, 
value-oriented phase of growth.India's oﬃce sector delivered a record-breaking performance in 2025, 
with leasing activity reaching an all-time high of approximately 82.6 mn 
sft,  marking the third consecutive year of record space take-up. New 
completions similarly scaled a new peak of 58.9 mn sft, up 10% 
year-on-year, with supply additions led by Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and 
Pune, which together accounted for nearly two-thirds of the year's new 
stock. Demand remained concentrated in India's gateway markets, 
with Bengaluru, Mumbai, and Delhi-NCR collectively driving around 
61% of total leasing activity for the year. Global Capability Centres 
(GCCs) continued to anchor the market's momentum, led decisively by 
Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and Delhi-NCR, underscoring India's 
deepening position as the preferred hub for global enterprises' 
innovation and delivery functions. Sustainability continued to gain 
ground as a market norm, with green-certiﬁed developments 
accounting for 93% of new supply and 75% of leasing activity during 
the year, reﬂecting the growing institutionalisation and ﬂight-to-quality 
shift deﬁning the sector. Overall, 2025 reaﬃrmed the oﬃce sector as 
one of the most resilient pillars of Indian real estate, underpinned by 
structural demand from global occupiers, sustained domestic 
consumption of Grade-A space, and a decisive pivot toward premium, 
ESG-compliant assets.India's real estate sector continued to strengthen its position as a core 
pillar of the economy with the broader "Financial, Real Estate, IT & 
Professional Services" category registering double-digit growth of 
10.4% in GVA terms as per MoSPI's provisional estimates, reﬂecting the 
sector's deepening contribution to national output. 
The residential real estate sector across India's top cities transitioned 
in FY 26 from a phase of volume-led expansion to one of value-led 
maturity. While housing sales volumes across the top seven cities 
moderated to approximately 3.95 lakh, the overall sales value crossed 
record highs, surging 6% annually to cross the INR 6 lakh crore mark, 
underscoring a decisive shift in homebuyer preference toward larger, 
higher-value conﬁgurations and premium products. Capital values 
across key markets registered strong appreciation, with average prices 
rising 8% year-on-year nationally, led by the National Capital Region at 
23% capital appreciation. A trend towards premiumisation in residential 
real estate has emerged over the past ﬁve years. This is clearly visible 
from the fact that for the ﬁrst time, units priced > INR 1.5 Cr have 
commanded a 42% share of total launches in contrast to their 9% share 
in 2020. The overarching trend across geographies was consistent: a 
market rewarding scale, execution credibility, and quality, conditions 
that favour organised, Grade-A developers.

Residential development remains the primary driver of our long-term 
growth. Our diversiﬁed portfolio spans apartments, villas, integrated 
townships and plotted developments across India's leading real estate 
markets, enabling us to address evolving homebuyer preferences 
while maintaining a geographically balanced development pipeline.
FY 26 was a landmark year for the residential business. We achieved 
our highest-ever pre-sales of ₹300,245 mn, representing a 76% 
year-on-year growth, while collections reached an all-time high of 
₹185,146 mn, reﬂecting robust customer demand and disciplined 
execution. The year also marked our successful entry into the NCR 
residential market with the launch of The Prestige City Indirapuram, 
further strengthening our national footprint.
As at FY 26, we had completed 163 residential projects aggregating 
144 mn sft, with 47 ongoing projects spanning 101 mn sft and 36 
upcoming projects covering 70 mn sft. Our development pipeline 
extends across Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, Mumbai, NCR, Kochi, 
Kozhikode, Mangaluru, Ooty, Goa, Mysore and Sakleshpur, providing 
strong visibility for future launches and execution.
Our residential pipeline, including upcoming projects and inventory, 
stood at ₹1,016,363 mn, while unrecognised revenue amounted to 
₹659,353 mn, providing visibility on future earnings. Estimated free 
cash ﬂows from the residential portfolio stood at ₹597,212 mn, 
supported by a land bank of 991 acres.
Looking ahead, our FY 27 launch pipeline comprises 58.12 mn sft with 
an estimated GDV of over ₹570,000 mn. During FY 26, we also added 
427 acres of land with a tentative GDV of ₹514,200 mn, reinforcing our 
ability to sustain long-term residential growth.Company Overview Operating Performance
At Prestige Estates Projects Limited (Prestige), every phase of our 
journey has been driven by a vision to evolve alongside India's 
changing urban landscape. What began as a real estate development 
business has, over nearly four decades, grown into one of India's 
leading integrated real estate companies, with a diversiﬁed presence 
across residential, commercial, retail and hospitality developments, 
supported by complementary capabilities that span the real estate 
value chain.
Today, our business extends beyond developing individual assets. We 
create integrated urban destinations that serve the evolving needs of 
homeowners, businesses, retailers and travellers. This diversiﬁed 
platform enables us to participate across multiple demand drivers 
while maintaining a balanced portfolio of development and annuity-led 
businesses.
Residential development remains the cornerstone of our business, with 
a portfolio spanning apartments, villas, integrated townships and 
plotted developments across India's key real estate markets. Our 
commercial portfolio comprises Grade A oﬃce parks, corporate 
campuses, built-to-suit developments, business parks and 
warehousing assets that cater to the evolving workspace requirements 
of global and domestic occupiers. In retail, we have created 
destinations that bring together shopping, dining, entertainment and 
culture, while our hospitality portfolio includes luxury hotels, resorts, 
convention centres, serviced residences and golf resorts that cater to 
both business and leisure travellers.
Supporting these businesses is an integrated ecosystem of capabilities 
that strengthens execution across the development lifecycle. Our 
property management arm ensures the eﬃcient operation and 
maintenance of completed developments, while our in-house 
construction, contracting, interiors, custom furniture and glazing 
businesses enhance execution eﬃciency, quality control and delivery 
timelines, reducing dependence on external partners while reinforcing 
operational excellence.
This integrated operating model gives us a distinct competitive 
advantage. Each business addresses a diﬀerent customer segment 
and market cycle, while together they enable us to develop large 
mixed-use destinations, optimise land utilisation and create value 
across the asset lifecycle. Today, with a presence across 13 cities, we 
continue to expand into markets with strong long-term fundamentals, 
supported by a development platform deﬁned by scale, execution 
excellence and diversiﬁcation.Integrated real estate platform

India's real estate sector is entering a phase of sustained structural

developers. Against this backdrop, we are well positioned to build on 
our strong development platform, diversiﬁed portfolio and expanding 
geographic footprint.
Our near-term focus remains on disciplined execution, timely project 
launches and prudent capital allocation. We are targeting 15-20%

attractive real estate markets.

Changes in land-use regulations, environmental norms, taxation and 
other regulatory frameworks, as well as delays in statutory approvals, 
could aﬀect project timelines, development costs and launch 
schedules.
Mitigation:  We maintain proactive engagement with regulatory 
authorities, adopt robust compliance and governance frameworks, and 
continuously monitor evolving regulations to facilitate timely approvals 
and minimise execution risks.Artiﬁcial Intelligence and Workplace Evolution Risk
The rapid adoption of artiﬁcial intelligence may reshape workplace 
models, space utilisation and employment patterns over the long term, 
potentially inﬂuencing demand for commercial oﬃce space and, 
indirectly, certain residential segments.
Mitigation: While AI is expected to transform the nature of work rather 
than eliminate the need for workplaces, we continuously monitor 
evolving occupier requirements and workplace trends to ensure our 
portfolio remains aligned with future demand. We design ﬂexible, 
future-ready Grade A oﬃce spaces, maintain a diversiﬁed portfolio 
across asset classes and geographies, and continue to deepen 
relationships with Global Capability Centres (GCCs) and multinational 
occupiers, enhancing the long-term resilience of our commercial 
business.
Land Acquisition and Business Development Risk 
Increasing competition for high-quality land parcels, rising acquisition 
costs and delays in securing development rights could impact future 
project pipelines and growth.
Mitigation:  We follow a disciplined business development strategy 
centred on rigorous due diligence, selective land acquisitions, joint 
development agreements (JDAs) and asset-light structures, enabling 
us to replenish our pipeline while maintaining capital eﬃciency.Market and Competitive Risk
Changes in economic conditions, customer sentiment, pricing 
dynamics and competitive intensity could inﬂuence sales velocity, 
leasing activity and proﬁtability across our portfolio.
Mitigation:  Our diversiﬁed presence across asset classes, customer 
segments and geographies reduces concentration risk. We remain 
focused on disciplined market selection, diﬀerentiated product 
oﬀerings, timely launches and execution excellence to sustain our 
competitive position.
Macroeconomic and Geopolitical Risk
Interest rate movements, inﬂation, currency volatility, geopolitical 
developments and broader economic uncertainties could impact 
customer demand, funding costs, supply chains and construction input 
prices.
Mitigation:  We maintain a prudent capital structure, diversify our 
funding sources and procurement channels, and continuously monitor 
macroeconomic developments to strengthen business resilience.
Capital and Liquidity Risk
Real estate development is inherently capital intensive and requires 
sustained access to ﬁnancing. Changes in liquidity conditions or 
ﬁnancing costs could aﬀect our ﬁnancial ﬂexibility and growth plans.
Mitigation:  We maintain disciplined capital allocation, healthy 
operating cash ﬂows and a diversiﬁed funding proﬁle while focusing on 
timely project execution, capital recycling and prudent leverage 
management.Climate and Environmental Risk
Climate change, including extreme weather events, rising 
temperatures, water stress and evolving environmental regulations, 
could aﬀect project execution, operating costs, asset performance and 
long-term value.
Mitigation:  We integrate sustainability into project planning through 
green building certiﬁcations, climate resilience assessments, energy- 
and water-eﬃcient design, and responsible resource management to 
enhance the resilience of our developments.
ESG and Sustainability Reporting Risk
Evolving ESG regulations and disclosure requirements, together with 
increasing expectations from investors, lenders and other 
stakeholders, could increase compliance obligations and reporting 
complexity.
Mitigation:  We continue to strengthen our ESG governance, 
sustainability reporting systems and data management processes 
while maintaining proactive engagement with investors, lenders, 
regulators and other stakeholders to ensure transparent and timely 
disclosures.Project Execution Risk
Large-scale developments are exposed to risks arising from labour 
availability, contractor performance, supply chain disruptions, raw 
material price volatility and the complexity of executing projects across 
multiple locations.
Mitigation:  We mitigate these risks through disciplined project 
planning, integrated execution capabilities, diversiﬁed procurement 
strategies, strong contractor relationships and continuous monitoring 
of project milestones, costs and timelines.
Technology and Cybersecurity Risk
Increasing digitalisation exposes the business to cybersecurity threats, 
technology failures and data privacy risks that could disrupt operations 
and impact stakeholder conﬁdence.
Mitigation:  We continue to strengthen our cybersecurity framework 
through technology upgrades, robust IT controls, business continuity 
planning, regular system monitoring and employee awareness 
programmes to safeguard critical systems and data.

Revenue from sale of real estate developments increased by 110.97% 
to ₹ 90,246 mn in FY 26, compared to ₹ 42,777 mn in FY 25 on account 
of completion and handover of residential projects launched in earlier 
years.
Revenue from sale of services has improved by 10.03% to ₹ 21,214 mn 
in FY 26 against ₹ 19,281 mn in FY 25 on account of improvement in 
hospitality and facility maintenance operations.
Revenue from lease rental has increased by 34.61% to ₹ 15,394 mn in 
FY 26 against ₹ 11,436 mn in FY 25 on account of leasing of space upon 
project completion and the impact of full year of operations for projects 
completed during the previous year.
Borrowing
Gross Borrowings have increased by 41.38% to ₹ 149,861 mn as at 31 
March 2026 against ₹ 106,002 mn as at 31 March 2025. The increase 
is attributable to the Company’s strategy to venture into new 
geographies and the acquisition of land parcels to ensure future 
growth of the Company.
Inventory
Inventory increased by 26.25% to ₹ 402,519 mn as at 31 March 2026 
against ₹ 318,831 mn as at 31 March 2025. The increase is attributable 
to an increase in construction activities along with the acquisition of 
land parcels to ensure future growth of the group and the acquisition of 
subsidiaries. Key Performance Ratios
Our key performance ratios reﬂected the strong operational 
momentum achieved during FY 26. Improved project execution and 
higher revenue recognition supported an expansion in net proﬁtability, 
while operating margins remained healthy despite changes in the 
project mix recognised during the year. The increase in the debt-equity 
ratio reﬂected continued investments in land acquisition and the 
development pipeline, consistent with our long-term growth strategy. 
The remaining ratios are presented above and further explain our 
liquidity, leverage and operational eﬃciency during the year.
Other income
Other income has increased by 32.12% to ₹ 5,101 mn in FY 26 against ₹ 
3,861 mn in FY 25 due to net gains on ﬁnancial assets designated as 
fair value through proﬁt or loss (FVPL) of ₹ 1,408 mn in FY 26 as against 
₹ 165 mn in FY 25.
Cost analysis
During the year, the total expenses increased by 65.28% to ₹ 114,648 
mn in FY 26 as against ₹ 69,367 mn in FY 25, primarily due to a

21.  CONSERVATION OF ENERGY, TECHNOLOGY ABSORPTION AND F OREIGN EXCHANGE EARNINGS AND 
OUTGO:
  The details of conservation of energy, technology absorption, foreign exchange earnings and outgo are as follows:
  The Company advances its sustainability agenda by integrating energy-eﬃcient practices and adopting innovative technologies that enhance 
performance, reduce environmental impact, and deliver long-term value. These initiatives align with Green Building principles, LEED standards, 
and the Energy Conservation Building Code, ensuring projects meet rigorous benchmarks while enhancing occupant well-being.
a) Conservation of Energy
Particulars Details
Steps taken or impact on 
conservation of energy  Increased the share of renewable electricity through oﬀ-site renewable energy procurement across 
operational sites.
 Installed on-site rooftop solar power systems to generate renewable electricity.
 Installed EV charging stations to promote sustainable mobility.
  Adopted energy-eﬃcient HVAC technologies, including auto tube chiller cleaning systems and direct 
drive power systems, to optimise energy consumption.
 Implemented IoT-enabled water monitoring systems to improve water use eﬃciency.
  Reused AHU condensate water for cooling tower operations to reduce freshwater consumption.
 Adopted zero water discharge practices and strengthened water reuse initiatives.
 Installed rainwater harvesting systems to augment water conservation.
 Installed Organic Waste Converters (OWCs) to process biodegradable waste into compost.
 Adopted sludge dewatering technology to convert STP sludge into manure.
  Enhanced green cover through Miyawaki forests, vertical gardens, tropical landscaping and native 
plantation initiatives.
 Implemented indoor air quality monitoring systems to enhance occupant well-being.
Steps taken by the 
company for utilising 
alternate sources of energy  Increased procurement of renewable electricity through oﬀ-site renewable energy Power Purchase 
Agreements (PPAs).
  Installed rooftop solar photovoltaic systems at select operational sites to generate clean energy.
  Continued to expand the share of renewable energy in the operational portfolio through a combination of 
oﬀ-site procurement and on-site solar generation.
b) Technology absorption
  We adopt advanced technologies to boost quality, sp eed 
processes, and reduce environmental impact, ensuring resource 
eﬃciency and resilience.
  Key measures include:
  •  Implemented IoT-enabled water monitoring systems to  
optimise water consumption.
  •  Adopted direct drive power systems to improve 
energy eﬃciency.
  •  Installed energy-eﬃcient auto tube chiller cleaning systems 
for HVAC optimisation.  •  Adopted advanced HVAC auto tube cooling systems to 
enhance operational eﬃciency.
  •  Implemented indoor air quality monitoring systems a cross 
operational sites.
 •  Installed multi-disc screw press technology to convert STP 
sludge into manure.
 •  Installed terrace-mounted solar panel grid systems for on-site 
renewable energy generation.
  These innovations enhance environmental performance  and 
create cost-eﬃcient, future ready spaces

CORPORATE GOVERNANCE REPORT
The PRESTIGE’s governance philosophy is built on the principles of integrity & transparency, accountability, sustainability and 
fostering stakeholder relationship
OUR PHILOSOPHY:
Our philosophy revolves around fostering sustainable practices that beneﬁt not only our Company but also the communities and environments in 
which we operate. We are committed to nurturing strong and meaningful relationships with our stakeholders that are built on trust, innovation and 
continuous improvement, coupled with transparent processes, drive our philosophy, propelling us to exceed expectations. Customer satisfaction lies 
at the heart of our philosophy, driving us to consistently deliver high-quality products and services that exceed expectations.

Corporate Governance
Corporate governance at our Company involves oversi ght by the 
Board of Directors and Committees, adherence to legal and regulatory 
frameworks, ethical business policies, transparent disclosures, rigorous 
risk and performance management. We prioritize disc losures and 
transparency, fostering accountability across all l evels of the organization.
Prestige adheres to governance policies and benchma rks 
through the following practices:
  Investor Presentation & Investor con calls:  Quarterly investor 
presentations provide updates on operational and fi nancial 
performance, project progress, launches, and other relevant 
details. Additionally, investors are engaged throug h con-calls, 
ensuring transparency in disclosure and operations.
  Quarterly review of internal control: There is a continuous 
eﬀort at Prestige to review and enhance internal co ntrols and 
risk mitigation strategies, fostering adherence to Corporate 
Governance principles.  Guidance vs. achievement:  T o maintain transparency and investor 
conﬁdence, the Company provides guidance on pre-sales at the 
start of each ﬁscal year. Quarterly evaluations com pare actual 
performance against these set targets.
We consider it our inherent responsibility to prote ct the rights of our 
shareholders and disclose timely, adequate and accu rate information 
regarding our ﬁnancials and performance, as well as the leadership and 
governance of the Company.
Code of Conduct
Prestige has embraced a robust code of conduct that  deﬁnes the 
organization’s mission, values and principles, link ing them with standards 
of professional conduct. This code articulates the values the organization 
wishes to foster in leaders and employees and, in d oing so, deﬁnes 
desired behaviour. As a result written codes of con duct and ethics 
has become benchmarks against which individual and organizational 
performance is measured.Governance Policies:

  Board Evaluation
  The Board of Directors has carried out an annual ev aluation of 
its own performance, board committees, and individual directors 
pursuant to the provisions of the Act and SEBI Listing Regulations. 
The performance of the board was evaluated by the Board after 
seeking inputs from all the directors on the basis of criteria such 
as the board composition and structure, eﬀectivenes s of board 
processes, information and functioning, etc.
  The performance of the committees was evaluated by the Board 
after seeking inputs from the committee members on the basis of 
criteria such as the composition of committees, eﬀectiveness of 
committee meetings, etc. The above criteria are broadly based on 
the Guidance Note on Board Evaluation issued by the Securities 
and Exchange Board of India on January 5, 2017.

call for a separate meeting of the Independent directors without

of management.  During the year under review, all the independent Directors of the Company met on March 26, 2026 without the presence of non-independent

  Prevention of Sexual Harassment of women at workplace
  The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Preven tion, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 is a leg islative act in India that aims to provide 
a safe working environment for women by preventing and addressing sexual harassment in the workplace. The Company strongly believes 
that all women must feel secure and valued at the workplace, and seeks to protect from the violations of their fundamental rights of gender 
equality, the right to life, right to life and the right to work with dignity, as established by the Indian Constitution.
  T o fulﬁl this criteria we have measures and policie s to prevent sexual harassment at work place. The C ompany has constituted Internal Complaints 
Committee in line with the Company’s policy on the Prevention, Prohibition & Redressal of Sexual Harassment at the Workplace
  During the ﬁnancial year, there were no complaints received from any employee.

     Terms of Reference:
     The Audit Committee of the Company is entrusted with the 
responsibility to supervise the Company’s internal controls 
and ﬁnancial reporting process and, inter alia, performs the 
following functions:
     •  superintending Company’s ﬁnancial reporting process  
and dissemination of ﬁnancial related information 
and to ensure that ﬁnancial statements are suﬃcient 
and credible;
     •  examining and reviewing annual ﬁnancial statements 
with management before submitting to the Board 
for approval;
     •  analyzing and reviewing management discussion and 
ﬁnancial position and results;
     •  analyzing and approving related party transactions in 
accordance with the policy of the Company;
     •  recommending the appointment, remuneration 
and terms of appointment of Statutory Auditors 
of the Company and approval for payment of any 
other services;
     •  reviewing and monitoring the auditor’s independence 
and performance, and eﬀectiveness of audit process;
     •  discussing with Statutory Auditors, before the 
commencement of audit, on the nature and scope 
of audit as well as having post-audit discussion to  
ascertain area of concern, if any;
     •  reviewing with management, Statutory Auditors 
and Internal Auditor, the adequacy of internal 
control systems;
     •  reviewing the ﬁnancial statements of subsidiaries i n 
particular, the investments made by them.     •  recommending appointment, remuneration and terms 
of appointment of Internal Auditor of the Company;
     •  reviewing the adequacy of internal audit function and 
discussing with Internal Auditor any signiﬁcant ﬁnding 
and reviewing the progress of corrective actions on  
such issues;
     •  evaluating internal financial controls and risk 
management systems;
     •  reviewing the functioning of the Whistle 
Blowing mechanism;
     •  giving guidance and directions under the SEBI 
(Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015
     •  reviewing, with the management, the statement of us es 
/ application of funds raised through an issue (public 
issue, rights issue, preferential issue, etc.), the  statement 
of funds utilized for purposes other than those stated 
in the oﬀer document / prospectus / notice and the 
report submitted by the monitoring agency monitoring 
the egularizat of proceeds of a public issue or rights 
issue or preferential issue or qualiﬁed institution s 
placement, and making appropriate recommendations 
to the board to take up steps in this matter;
     • scrutiny of inter-corporate loans and investments;
     •  valuation of undertakings or assets of the listed entity, 
wherever it is necessary;
     •  approval of appointment of chief ﬁnancial oﬃcer 
after assessing the qualiﬁcations, experience and 
background, etc. of the candidate;
     •  reviewing the utilization of loans and/ or advances  from/
investment by the holding company in the subsidiary 
exceeding rupees 100 crore or 10% of the asset size 
of the subsidiary, whichever is lower including existing 
loans / advances / investments existing as on the date 
of coming into force of this provision.
     •  consider and comment on rationale, cost-beneﬁts 
and impact of schemes involving merger, demerger, 
amalgamation etc., on the listed entity and 
its shareholders.

Risk Management Committee
   Risk Management Committee consists of all the members of 
the Board (except Ms. Neelam Chhiber).
   Terms of Reference of Risk Management Committee are 
as follows:
   •  The functional heads shall identify and analyze all the 
material risks, both external and internal as far as their 
department is concerned and report the Risks along 
with their assessment of Risks which are beyond the 
Risk Tolerance level to the RMC.
     •  RMC would consolidate the views expressed by the 
functional heads and also provide for mitigation of  
such risks and it shall report to the Audit Committee of 
the Company in the form of an action plan.
     •  The Audit Committee is bestowed with the duty of 
considering the information as placed by the RMC and delineate it to the Board along with its comments and 
reviews thereon.
     •  The Board’s role is to ensure framing, implementing  
and monitoring risk management plan, having in place 
systems for risk management as part of internal con trols 
with duty being cast upon Independent Directors to 
bring unbiased angle to the Board’s deliberations on 
making risk management systems more robust.
     •  All other employees are also equally responsible to  
alert any possible Risks and to raise Risks they have 
identiﬁed with their managers or directly with the 
functional heads.
     •  To periodically review the risk management policy 
by considering the changing industry dynamics and 
evolving complexity.

 c.  Vigil Mechanism and Whistle Blower Policy:
    We at Prestige are committed to conducting business  in 
accordance with applicable laws, rules and regulati ons 
and the highest standards of business ethics and to  full 
and accurate disclosures. The Company believes in the conduct of the aﬀairs of its constituents in a fair and 
transparent manner by adopting highest standards of  
professionalism, honesty, integrity and ethical beh aviour. 
The purpose of this mechanism is to eliminate and help to 
prevent malpractices, to investigate and resolve complaints, 
take appropriate action to safeguard the interests of the 
Company and to ensure that any person making a comp laint 
(referred to as “a whistleblower”) is protected, while at the 
same time actively discouraging frivolous and insubstantial 
complaints. Company oversees the vigil mechanism th rough 
Audit committee.
   This mechanism has been communicated to all 
concerned and posted on the Company’s website www.
prestigeconstructions.com

 f.   Compliance of Prohibition of Insider Trading 
Regulations:
   As per the provisions of the SEBI (Prohibition of I nsider 
Trading) Regulations, 2015, your Company adopted a Code 
of Conduct for prevention of Insider trading in the securities 
(“Insider Trading Code”) to regulate, monitor and r eport trading by designated persons in securities of the Company. 
The Insider Trading Code has been implemented to prevent 
the misuse of unpublished price-sensitive informati on and 
set a framework, rules, and procedures that all concerned 
parties should follow, both in letter and spirit, while trading in 
listed or proposed to be listed securities of the C ompany. The 
policy and procedures are periodically reviewed and  revised 
from time to time and communicated to the designate d 
persons. A digital platform is being maintained by the 
Company, which contains the names and other prescribed 
particulars of the persons covered under the Insider Trading 
Code. This online tracking mechanism helps with mon itoring 
trade in the Company’s securities by designated per sons 
and taking appropriate action in case of any violation/non-
compliance of the Company’s Insider Trading Code

 s.  Transfer of unclaimed/unpaid amounts to the Investor Education and Protection Fund (“IEPF”) 
  Pursuant to Sections 124 and 125 of the Act read with the Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority (Accounting, Audit, Transfer and 
Refund) Rules, 2016 (“IEPF Rules”), dividends, if not claimed for a period of seven years from the date of transfer to Unpaid Dividend Account 
of the Company, are liable to be transferred to IEPF.
  Further, all the shares in respect of which dividend has remained unclaimed for seven consecutive years or more from the date of transfer to 
unpaid dividend account shall also be transferred to IEPF Authority.
  The above requirement does not apply to shares in r espect of which there is a speciﬁc order of Court, Tribunal or Statutory Authority, restraining 
any transfer of the shares.
  In the interest of the Members, the Company sends periodical reminders to claim their dividends in order to avoid transfer of dividends/shares 
to IEPF Authority.
  The details of unclaimed dividends, shares liable to be transferred to the IEPF Authority and their due date for transfer are uploaded on the 
Company’s website at www.prestigeconstructions.com .
  The Shareholders, who have so far not claimed the dividend for the ﬁnancial year 2018-19 or any subsequent years, are requested to submit 
their claim to the Company’s Registrar and Transfer Agent.
